The **Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine** ([Swedish](Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Nobelpriset i fysiologi eller medicin*) is awarded yearly by the [Nobel Assembly](Nobel_Assembly_at_the_Karolinska_Institute "Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institute") at the [Karolinska Institute](Karolinska_Institute "Karolinska Institute") for outstanding discoveries in [physiology](Physiology "Physiology") or medicine. The [Nobel Prize](Nobel_Prize "Nobel Prize") is not a single prize, but five separate prizes that, according to [Alfred Nobel](Alfred_Nobel "Alfred Nobel")'s 1895 will, are awarded "to those who, during the preceding year, have conferred the greatest benefit to humankind". Nobel Prizes are awarded in the fields of [Physics](Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics"), [Chemistry](Nobel_Prize_in_Chemistry "Nobel Prize in Chemistry"), Physiology or Medicine, [Literature](Nobel_Prize_in_Literature "Nobel Prize in Literature"), and [Peace](Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize").

The Nobel Prize is presented annually on the anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death, 10 December. As of 2022, 114 Nobel Prizes in Physiology or Medicine have been awarded to 226 laureates, 214 men and 12 women. The first one was awarded in 1901 to the German physiologist, [Emil von Behring](Emil_von_Behring "Emil von Behring"), for his work on [serum](Blood_plasma "Blood plasma") therapy and the development of a [vaccine](Vaccine "Vaccine") against [diphtheria](Diphtheria "Diphtheria"). The first woman to receive the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, [Gerty Cori](Gerty_Cori "Gerty Cori"), received it in 1947 for her role in elucidating the metabolism of [glucose](Glucose "Glucose"), important in many aspects of medicine, including treatment of [diabetes](Diabetes "Diabetes"). The most recent Nobel prize was announced by the Karolinska Institute on 3 October 2022, and has been awarded to Swedish [Svante Pääbo](Svante_P%C3%A4%C3%A4bo "Svante Pääbo"), for the discoveries concerning the genomes of extinct hominins and human evolution.[[2]](Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine#cite_note-2)

The prize consists of a medal along with a diploma and a certificate for the monetary award. The [front side](Obverse "Obverse") of the medal displays the same profile of [Alfred Nobel](Alfred_Nobel "Alfred Nobel") depicted on the medals for Physics, Chemistry, and Literature; the reverse side is unique to this medal.

Some awards have been controversial. This includes one to [António Egas Moniz](Ant%C3%B3nio_Egas_Moniz "António Egas Moniz") in 1949 for the [prefrontal lobotomy](Lobotomy "Lobotomy"), bestowed despite protests from the medical establishment. Other controversies resulted from disagreements over who was included in the award. The 1952 prize to [Selman Waksman](Selman_Waksman "Selman Waksman") was litigated in court, and half the patent rights were awarded to his co-discoverer [Albert Schatz](Albert_Schatz_(scientist) "Albert Schatz (scientist)") who was not recognised by the prize. Nobel prizes cannot be awarded posthumously. Also, no more than three recipients can receive a Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, a limitation that is sometimes discussed as an increasing trend for larger teams to conduct important scientific projects.

The **2021 [Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine](Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine "Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine")** was jointly awarded to the American physiologist [David Julius](David_Julius "David Julius") (b. 1955) and Armenian-American neuroscientist [Ardem Patapoutian](Ardem_Patapoutian "Ardem Patapoutian") (b. 1967) "for the discovery of [receptors](Sensory_receptor "Sensory receptor") for temperature and [touch](Touch "Touch")."[[2]](2021_Nobel_Prize_in_Physiology_or_Medicine#cite_note-2) During the award ceremony on December 10, 2021, Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet member Patrik Ernfors expressed:



> "The 2021 Nobel Prize laureates have explained fundamental mechanisms underpinning how we sense the world within and around us.
